claims.statement: .openwikiignore preserves authored documentation, specifications, tooling, templates, and useful assets as research inputs while excluding rendered outputs, exports, local environments, caches, and secrets; OpenWiki documentation and metadata remain writable.

Sphinx recognizes only .rst sources and uses hub/index as master_doc; CommonMark packages in requirements do not enable Markdown sources, and the partner .rstx form is consumed explicitly by Pandoc instead.

The site navigation is an authored graph: hub/index combines visible panels with a hidden toctree, index-developer routes to the main references, and learning/building-block landing pages also pair cards with hidden trees.
Root index.rst is an orphan document rather than the configured master, and conf.py explicitly maps index.html to hub/index.html along with literal redirects for several legacy reference URLs.

Explicit configuration and DTL labels connect reference definitions to :ref: links, quick-reference tables, and panel link-buttons, so label changes affect consumers independently of filenames and heading wording.

Authored document links include relative :doc: paths as well as panel URL buttons containing literal .html filenames; navigation review therefore must consider document paths and literal URLs as well as section labels.
The web partner agreement and Pandoc partner form share partner-agreement-part-1.rst and partner-agreement-part-2.rst through includes, coupling website wording to the printable agreement.
Databrowser authentication and GDPR platform configuration include the same authentication-provider RST fragment, which carries a databrowser end-of-life warning for December 31st 2023.
Time-based masterdata management and parameterized datatype pattern pages use start-h3/end-h3 substitutions defined as raw HTML heading markup, making that presentation builder-sensitive.
Sphinx configures version and release substitution values as x.y and 2024; these are documentation configuration values rather than a runtime-version discovery mechanism.

Service API documentation renders local Node and Portal Swagger 2.0 YAML copies through openapi directives, while the databrowser guide renders its own local Swagger YAML; the directives do not fetch live specifications.
The databrowser Swagger specification scopes its endpoints to internal use and explicitly permits them to change or be removed at any time.

Orphan status does not make root sources unused: Community is linked by the navbar, Legal has a policy tree and download links, and orphan legal-service, legal-dap, and partner fragments participate in legal composition.

Configuration maintenance starts at index-service-configuration and follows general, pipe, and system guides containing common prototypes/property tables into type-specific source, sink, transform, pump, and system references; quick-reference and feature links are coupled consumers.

DTL maintenance spans the landing-page toctree, grouped operator references with labels/argument notation/examples, annotated examples, transform configuration, and quick-reference links rather than a single monolithic source.
Connector documentation separates the connector input/output contract from configurable manifest, templates, and config.json building blocks, linked from the connector guide.

Tutorial source changes can affect navigation and authored download inputs: learning/getting-started pages link tutorial guides, Collect Data downloads CSVs under hub/files, and baseline upload downloads JSON with an explicit configuration-overwrite warning.

The local README documents creating and activating a Python 3 virtual environment, installing pip/wheel/requirements, running make html, and opening _build/html/index.html or using python3 -m http.server for search summaries.

The dependency toolchain is pinned, including Sphinx 4.5.0, pydata-sphinx-theme 0.8.0, docutils 0.16, OpenAPI 0.7.0, and panels 0.6.0; the README states a Python 3.7 theme minimum, CI selects Python 3.9/Ubuntu 22.04, and the root builder selects Python 3.8.12/Bullseye.

conf.py directly indexes os.environ['VIRTUAL_ENV'] to build exclusions, so the key must exist even without a real virtual environment; CI supplies venv and the root Dockerfile supplies an empty string.

Normal Unix make html requires Pandoc and TeX contract-generation tools in addition to Python/Sphinx; README platform hints differ from the CI recipes, which install a broader TeX/font/Ghostscript set and Pandoc 2.13.

The Unix Makefile defaults SPHINXOPTS to -W, checks for sphinx-build, builds from the repository root with _build/doctrees, and writes HTML to _build/html; explicitly clearing SPHINXOPTS removes the default warning-as-error option.

Unix html depends on SaaS PDF/DOCX and partner DOCX generation before Sphinx: the SaaS recipe combines terms, service description, pricing, and DPA via Pandoc JSON with appendix headings, while partnerdocx consumes the included RSTX form; privacy policy is linked by Legal but absent from that SaaS assembly.
pagebreak.lua preserves TeX output while converting raw newpage/pagebreak commands and standalone form-feed paragraphs into target-specific page breaks, including OpenXML for DOCX.
Generated contract downloads under files and the _build directory are ignored outputs; the Makefile derives the contracts from authored legal inputs rather than using exported PDF/DOCX as sources.

Despite the README's without-SaaS wording, html_no_saas only touches three download paths and runs the same HTML build, with no Pandoc conversion or SaaS source exclusion/tag; missing files become empty placeholders and existing files are not regenerated.

The Unix Makefile offers alternative Sphinx builders directly without html's legal-generation prerequisites; LaTeX PDF and Info targets add external tool steps, and gettext uses a separate environment rather than shared doctrees.
LaTeX, man-page, and Texinfo document lists are commented out in conf.py, so exposed targets alone do not establish a configured and verified alternative release artifact.

make.bat is not equivalent to Unix make html: it does not default SPHINXOPTS to -W, has a Python-module fallback for missing sphinx-build, invokes HTML directly, and lacks the Unix contract-generation, html_no_saas, and Docker targets.
External-link validation is available through make linkcheck with output at _build/linkcheck/output.txt, but neither inspected PR nor master workflow invokes it.
Doctest and coverage targets are advertised conditionally, but conf.py enables neither sphinx.ext.doctest nor sphinx.ext.coverage, so these are not an enabled documentation test suite.

The PR workflow runs on pull_request and validates through make html with contract tools and VIRTUAL_ENV=venv; it has no image publishing/deployment step, and the PR/master workflows contain no separate schema-validation, lint, or example-execution step.

HTML presentation is wired through pydata_sphinx_theme, _templates, _static/css/custom.css, logo/favicon assets, configured search/navigation sidebars, and custom navbar/footer options; enabled extensions provide OpenAPI, panels, not-found pages, copy buttons, redirects, argparse, and Jinja.

The layout template extends the upstream layout and defines footer/body overrides, analytics/marketing embeds, and conditional breadcrumbs; its exclusions compare bare page names rather than hub-prefixed document names, while breadcrumb links use pathto(master_doc) and parent links.

Custom navigation has deployment-path assumptions: the right menu links Community through /community.html plus external Support/Sign up links, the footer links Legal/Terms to the public docs host, and a separate template supplies ISO footer text.

custom.css imports remote fonts and overrides responsive navigation, breadcrumbs, sidebars, cards/buttons, code tables, and footer styling; source-linked figures and downloads also exist outside _static, such as databrowser-guide-images and hub/files.

The older _static/custom.js copy-button code depends on jQuery and Clipboard, but conf.py does not register that asset via html_js_files and instead enables sphinx_copybutton; asset presence alone does not establish activation.

The publishing workflow is triggered by any push to master, sets DOCKER_BUILD_PUSH=1, defaults TAG to latest, and runs make html followed by make docker; docker depends on html, so the second command traverses the HTML dependency again.

make docker stages _build/html under docker/dist/html and cleans staging only after build.sh succeeds; failed build/push can leave staging, while Unix make clean removes _build output and docker/dist but not files contract downloads.

docker/build.sh is fail-fast, defaults to building but not pushing, and exposes TAG, IMAGE_NAME, DOCKER_BUILD, DOCKER_BUILD_PUSH, and DOCKER_BUILD_OPTIONS as controls; master enables push after registry authentication.

Master publication retags and pushes the serving image to ACR with both the selected tag and github.sha, authenticates to Azure, and requests deployment of the SHA-tagged image using acrName, containerAppName, resourceGroup, and imageToDeploy; credential inputs are DOCKER_PASSWORD, ACR_PASSWORD, and AZURE_CREDENTIALS.

The root Dockerfile supplies a Python/Pandoc/TeX build environment in /docs, installs requirements, defines VIRTUAL_ENV empty, and defaults to make html, but copies only requirements rather than the authored source tree; inspected CI prepares its toolchain on the runner.

The docker-directory Dockerfile instead builds the nginx serving image from staged dist files; nginx listens on port 80 and serves static HTML with internal 404/50x error pages, separate from Sphinx's redirect map and configured notfound extension.

Managed OpenWiki updates run daily at cron 0 8 * * * or manual dispatch with content/PR write permissions, full-history checkout for update diffs, Node.js 22, OpenWiki 0.7.2, and optional Mermaid/jsdom validation dependencies; provider/authentication/tracing settings are environment inputs.

OpenWiki update automation deliberately continues after update-command failure, removes transient .run.json, creates a scoped openwiki/update PR containing wiki/managed-navigation/workflow paths and conditional CLAUDE.md, preserves completed-page progress, then propagates the failure unless cancelled before the relevant steps.

AGENTS.md makes the generated wiki optional just-in-time context and directs normal contributors to update source code/docs rather than hand-edit generated pages unless explicitly asked, keeping managed wiki updates distinct from authored Sphinx maintenance.
